page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL4 is a KVM-based virtual server featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. It provides 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 48 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25%. The system excels in memory bandwidth for large blocks, achieving 251.6 GB/sec read and 111.91 GB/sec write speeds. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform exceptionally well, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression reaching top-tier thresholds. In LLM inference tests, the server demonstrates top-tier capabilities, processing 2806.44 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 54.33 tokens/sec for text generation on a medium 7B model.

The hardware profile presents specific architectural tradeoffs. While the CPU allocation is shared, the AMD EPYC 9575F core architecture maintains high single-threaded efficiency. The absence of local storage requires users to attach external block storage for persistent data, which may impact sequential I/O-heavy workloads. Qualitatively, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with dual enterprise-grade GPUs offers a cost-efficient platform for memory-intensive parallel computing without the overhead of a larger vCPU footprint.

This configuration is highly suited for machine learning workloads, specifically medium-scale LLM inference, model fine-tuning, and image processing. The combination of 192 GB of RAM and dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs also makes it appropriate for data science pipelines, parallelized scientific simulations, and high-throughput web serving environments that require GPU acceleration.
